summary.headline: Wakefit Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19.9% YoY to INR452 crore, a record quarter, with reported PAT of INR15.9 crore hit by a deferred tax charge.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR452 crore (+19.9% YoY), the company's highest ever quarter, with reported EBITDA of INR50.2 crore (11.1% margin) and reported PAT of INR15.9 crore. Gross margin compressed to 53.9% from 57.7% as crude-linked raw material costs stayed elevated, and management passed through price increases while protecting absolute rupee profitability. The festive sale start moved from late September last year to 8 October this year, shifting part of festive demand into Q3. Store additions reached 205 (137 cities) at 30 September, and management said H2 store additions will moderate but FY27 will exceed the original 80-store target.

segments.name: Mattresses
segments.commentary: 61.8% of Q2 revenue, growing 21.4% YoY; management expects steady growth from omnichannel expansion. Mattress volume grew in the mid-teens in July-August, with value growth higher due to price increases. FY26 mattress volume was about 915,000 units, split roughly 50:50 between H1 and H2.

segments.name: Furniture
segments.commentary: 30.1% of Q2 revenue, growing 24.9% YoY, faster than mattresses. Growth was tepid in Q1 due to a machine breakdown and labour issues, which management says are resolved; it expects acceleration as jumbo stores open.

segments.name: Furnishings
segments.commentary: 8.1% of Q2 revenue and the weakest category. Management blamed a leadership vacuum after the category head left about 6-9 months ago; growth returned to normal in July-September, with no growth figure given.

segments.name: Own channels (website + COCO stores)
segments.commentary: About 70% of Q2 revenue versus 60.2% in Q2 FY26, growing about 39.4% YoY. Repeat customers were over 32% of revenue, and the average cart held close to 2 products.

segments.name: Retail network
segments.commentary: 205 company-owned company-operated stores in 137 cities at 30 September, up from 165 stores in 100 cities at 30 June; 68 stores added in H1 and 41 in Q2. About 110 are mega stores and 95 mini stores (about 1,000 sq ft). MBO network is 2,589 outlets across 787 cities, up from about 2,250 in 701 cities.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company-owned store additions will exceed the original target of 80 (H2 additions to moderate); the final number to be given in the next call.
FY27 capex of INR100-120 crore, with about 80% on retail expansion including jumbo stores and about 20% on manufacturing, automation and upgrades.
Rent expense guided at INR90-92 crore for FY27 (vs INR84 crore last year).
A&P spend guided at 7-8% of revenue for the full year, implying H2 above H1's roughly 6%.
Management said it is tracking to the Board-approved annual operating plan and expects growth to stay in line with Q2's rate; no specific revenue or margin percentage given.
Deferred tax charges expected to continue for the next couple of quarters and into FY28; deferred tax at about 20-25% of PBT, with total tax at about 35-40%.
Brought-forward tax losses expected to be fully used by Q2 or Q3 FY28.
No further price increases are planned barring unforeseen crude spikes.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex cash outflow about INR60-65 crore, of which COCO stores about INR25-30 crore; FY26 full-year capex about INR30 crore.
Jumbo store in Bengaluru under construction, with launch targeted for Q2 FY28; it will have 1.2-1.3 lakh sq ft of retail space and a cost above INR50 crore per store including display inventory.
Management expects jumbo store payback close to 2 years versus under 1 year for mini and mega stores; rent for the jumbo store is said to be only a few lakh rupees a month.
Mini stores (about 1,000 sq ft) and mega stores have payback under one year; mega stores need 1.5-2x the investment of mini stores.
Stores take 2-4 months to stabilise after opening, which is why H1 front-loading is expected to boost H2 revenue.
About INR400 crore cash before the IPO plus INR377 crore raised; cash is earmarked for factory base, inorganic acquisitions and jumbo store scale-up, to be deployed over about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Festive sale started around 8 October 2026 versus 22 September 2025; management said the sale was decent but not spectacular given moderate discretionary spending.
Pre-sale period comparison: value up in the mid-20s% and volume up in the late teens% YoY.
Like-for-like same-store sales grew in the mid-teens% for stores in existence.

Price increases since the war began in March 2026: about 10-11% average ASP increase (per CFO), with one price cut in between. Raw material costs are up about 30-60% versus pre-war levels (CFO cited about 40% average), and the RM share of COGS drove an ASP increase of about 11%.
CFO said absolute rupee gross margin per unit is similar to pre-March 2026, though percentage margin is lower.
Own-channel vs external split guided at about 70-72% own and 25-28% external; external marketplaces and quick commerce still drive new-customer acquisition during sales.
Raw material availability has eased, but prices remain elevated; the company does not buy at spot prices and has secured supply via relationships across plants and geographies.
Competition: management says the company is distinct from franchise-run EBOs of traditional mattress brands because all its COCO stores are staffed by employees.

qa_highlights.question: What was the like-for-like growth before the festive sale shift, and how is the festive period going?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-sale comparison showed value up in the mid-20s% and volume in the late teens%. Like-for-like same-store sales grew in the mid-teens%. Festive sale was decent, but not spectacular.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further price hikes or raw material softening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not plan more price hikes barring unforeseen crude rises. Raw material availability has eased, but prices remain 30-60% above pre-war levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the A&P outlook for H2, and is the 7-8% guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is sticking with the 7-8% full-year guidance because the OND sale period carries heavy spend. The company tracks a broader measure that includes store opex.

qa_highlights.question: Why is rent guided higher, and what drives the change in per-store rent?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 rent is guided at INR90-92 crore, including warehouses and offices. Per-store rent fell as mini stores (about 1,000 sq ft) replaced mega stores (about 3,500 sq ft): 110 mega and 95 mini stores at 30 September versus about 30 mini stores at March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company holding a large cash pile, and what is the deployment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-IPO cash was about INR400 crore, with INR377 crore raised. Plans for a factory, acquisitions and jumbo stores have moved more slowly than expected, and deployment is planned over about 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How is the jumbo store economics different, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Each jumbo store costs over INR50 crore including display inventory. Payback is targeted at close to 2 years, with supply-chain savings and a larger catalogue as drivers. Bengaluru launch is targeted for Q2 FY28.

risks_watch: Gross margin fell 380 bps YoY to 53.9%; raw material costs remain elevated and price increases are capped by demand elasticity.
Reported PAT was held back by a INR6.5 crore deferred tax charge; the effective tax rate was about 40% in Q2, and deferred tax will continue for several quarters.
Furnishings growth is still soft after a leadership vacuum, and recovery depends on the category head filled recently.
Store productivity: new stores take 2-4 months to stabilise, and H1 front-loading relies on H2 maturity; retail growth (24%) is close to total mattress growth.
Discretionary demand is moderate, and the festive shift makes Q2 vs Q3 comparisons hard; management will assess underlying trends on H1 plus Q3 together.
key_quotes: For quarter 2 FY27, revenue from operations stood at INR452 crores, our highest ever quarterly revenue, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 19.9%.

We won't be able to provide a very specific percentage on revenue and margin, but happy to share that we are tracking well towards the annual operating plan that we had shared with the Board and got approvals.

However, we don't believe that we want to do any more additional price hikes because we've always been treading the fine line between growth and destroying volume growth -- value growth versus destroying volume growth.
In terms of the absolute rupee gross margin per unit, yes, it is similar.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the underlying business: management repeatedly stressed record revenue, protected absolute rupee profitability and the Board-approved plan. It was cautious and evasive on forward numbers, declining to give revenue or margin percentages for H2, a store-count figure, volume splits, and channel-level online/offline data, while giving firm answers on capex, rent, tax and A&P guidance.

rows.label: Jumbo store format (Bengaluru)
